Thiruvananthapuram: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a yellow alert in several Kerala districts, forecasting isolated heavy rainfall on November 4, 6, 7 and 8. The warning comes amid changing weather conditions over parts of south India, with a depression over Telangana and coastal Andhra Pradesh and cyclonic circulations over the Lakshadweep region and Tamil Nadu.
Yellow alert in eight districts
According to the IMD's latest forecast issued at 1 pm on Wednesday (November 4), isolated heavy rainfall is likely in the following districts:
November 4: Kottayam, Idukki and Wayanad
November 6: Idukki and Ernakulam
November 7: Pathanamthitta and Kottayam
November 8: Alappuzha, Kottayam and Ernakulam
A yellow alert indicates the possibility of isolated heavy rainfall, with precipitation expected to range between 64.5 mm and 115.5 mm in 24 hours.
The IMD said a depression was located over eastern Telangana and coastal Andhra Pradesh on Wednesday. It is likely to move northwards and weaken into a well-marked low-pressure area within the next six hours.
Two cyclonic circulations are also influencing the weather. One is located over Lakshadweep and adjoining areas, while the other is over southern Tamil Nadu.
The weather department has forecast isolated heavy rainfall, with precipitation of 7 cm to 11 cm in 24 hours, on November 4, 6, 7 and 8.
Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and strong winds are also likely in Kerala between November 4 and 8. Wind speeds could reach 30-40 kmph.
Will schools and colleges remain closed on November 5?
The current IMD forecast does not indicate the possibility of school or college holidays in any Kerala district on Thursday, November 5, as no district is under a heavy rainfall alert for that day.
However, weather conditions could change. If heavy or more intense rainfall is forecast in the coming hours, decisions on closing educational institutions will depend on the conditions in the respective areas.
Any holiday will be announced only through official orders issued by district collectors or other competent authorities.
Students and parents have been advised to follow official announcements from district administrations and notices issued by their educational institutions for updates on holidays or changes to class schedules.
